summary.text: Dan Meuser is the Republican incumbent for Pennsylvania's 9th District, first elected in 2018 and sworn in in 2019. He spent decades at Pride Mobility Products, a power mobility manufacturer, where he served as president of Pride USA, and was Pennsylvania Secretary of Revenue from 2011 to 2015. In Congress he serves on the Financial Services and Small Business committees and chairs the Financial Services Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations.

paragraphs.text: According to his official biography, Meuser is the son of a police officer and attended New York Maritime University and Cornell University, where he was in the Navy ROTC program.
He earned a bachelor's degree from Cornell University in 1986.

In 1988 he joined Pride Mobility Products, a healthcare products manufacturer that, according to his official biography, he helped grow into an industry leader in power mobility products, and he served as president of Pride USA for seven years.
Meuser served as Pennsylvania Secretary of Revenue from 2011 to 2015 under Gov. Tom Corbett, a Republican.
His official biography says the Council on State Taxation rated the department as the most improved in the country during his tenure.
Meuser won the open 9th District seat on November 6, 2018, defeating Democrat Denny Wolff, and was sworn in as a member of the 116th Congress in 2019.
He serves on the House Financial Services Committee, where he chairs the Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations, and on the Small Business Committee.
He is a member of the Problem Solvers Caucus, Main Street Caucus, Republican Study Committee and Border Security Caucus, and co-chair of the Congressional Coal Caucus.
According to his official biography, he lives in Luzerne County with his wife, Shelley, and they have two daughters and a son.
